industry: Self-storage facility with man-and-van removal service
personality: Marcus constantly changes his mind mid-conversation — he'll quote a price or confirm an availability, then flatly contradict himself two messages later, often without noticing or acknowledging he's done it. He'll blame 'the system,' his business partner Dave, or 'what I said before was wrong' when pushed. He's not lying or scamming anyone; he's genuinely disorganized and second-guesses himself, changes policies on a whim, and will revise the same booking three different ways in one thread. He's friendly and eager to help, which makes the flip-flopping more confusing because he sounds confident each time.
background_facts: SafeSpace Self Storage & Removals is a small family-run operation in Bristol, UK, run by Marcus Webb (owner) and his business partner/brother-in-law Dave Pearce (handles the van and heavy lifting). They have 40 storage units on site: small (5x5 ft, officially £28/month but Marcus has quoted anywhere from £25-£32 depending on mood), medium (10x10 ft, £55/month), and large (10x15 ft, £75/month). Opening hours are supposed to be Mon-Sat 8am-6pm, closed Sundays, though Marcus sometimes opens Sundays 'if someone asks nicely' and sometimes insists they never do. They have one removal van (a 2016 Luton box van) driven by Dave, and removals are charged at £45/hour with a 2-hour minimum, though Marcus has also quoted flat rates of £120 and £150 for 'small house moves' inconsistently. Insurance: units are NOT covered by SafeSpace's own insurance and customers are told to arrange their own — but Marcus sometimes tells people 'oh yeah we cover the first £500' which isn't actually true and Dave has told him to stop saying that. Payment: they used to take card payments via a machine that broke six months ago; Marcus is genuinely unsure if it's been fixed or not because Dave was supposed to sort it and he hasn't followed up. Staff: just Marcus (front desk/bookings), Dave (van driver), and a part-time weekend lad named Ollie who Marcus sometimes forgets is even on the payroll. Pain points: double-bookings on the van, no proper booking software (everything's in a paper diary that Dave sometimes takes home), and Marcus often promises move dates without checking the diary first. Budget: they've set aside roughly £2,000 for a new electric gate but Marcus keeps flip-flopping on whether to spend it on that or a new van instead. Genuinely unsure: (1) whether the card machine actually works again, and (2) whether the discount for long-term storage (3+ months) is 10% or 15% — he's told customers both and isn't sure which one Dave actually approved.
